name: Goals
short: Goals a player scores, credited to the last player on the scoring team to touch the puck. It's the stat every other number on this site is trying to predict.
primaryKeyword: what does g mean in hockey

name: Assists
short: Credit for the last one or two players on the scoring team to touch the puck before the goal scorer. The first is the primary assist, the second the secondary.
primaryKeyword: what does a mean in hockey

name: Points
short: Goals plus assists, each worth one point. It's the standard way to rank skaters, and it counts a secondary assist the same as a goal.

name: Plus-minus
short: Goals for minus goals against while a skater is on the ice at even strength or shorthanded. Power-play goals don't count, and it can't tell who caused the goal.
primaryKeyword: what is plus minus in hockey

name: Penalty minutes
short: Total minutes a player is penalized, at two for a minor, five for a major and 10 for a misconduct. Penalties he draws don't offset it.

name: Power-play goals and points
short: Goals (PPG) and points (PPP) scored while the other team is shorthanded by a penalty. They show who a coach trusts with the man advantage.

name: Shorthanded goals and points
short: Goals (SHG) and points (SHP) scored while a player's own team is shorthanded by a penalty. They're rare and swing a lot from one season to the next.
primaryKeyword: what does shg mean in hockey

name: Even-strength goals
short: Goals (EVG) and points (EVP) scored when neither team is shorthanded by a penalty, including 4-on-4, 3-on-3 and most empty-net goals. Most scoring happens here.

name: Game-winning goals
short: The goal that put the winner one ahead of the loser's final total, so the third goal of a 5-2 win. It can come in the first period.

name: Overtime goals
short: Goals scored in overtime, which end the game on the spot. Regular-season overtime is five minutes of 3-on-3; playoff overtime is full 20-minute periods at five-on-five.

name: Shots on goal
short: Goals plus the shots a goalie stopped. Misses, posts and blocked shots don't count, so it's the narrowest of the shot stats.
primaryKeyword: what does sog mean in hockey

name: Shooting percentage
short: Goals divided by shots on goal. A shooter who runs far above his career rate in one season usually drifts back toward it the next.
primaryKeyword: what is shooting percentage in hockey

name: Time on ice
short: How many minutes a player is on the ice, in total or per game (ATOI). It's the clearest read on how much a coach trusts someone.
primaryKeyword: what does toi mean in hockey

name: Faceoff percentage
short: Faceoffs won divided by faceoffs taken (FOW counts the wins). 50% is break-even, and the best regular centers win around 60%.

name: Hits
short: Body checks credited by each arena's off-ice scorers, who don't all count them the same way. A team that's hitting a lot usually doesn't have the puck.
primaryKeyword: what does hits mean in hockey

name: Blocked shots
short: Opponents' shot attempts a skater stops with his body or stick before they reach the net. A team that blocks a lot is usually defending a lot.

name: Takeaways and giveaways
short: Takeaways (TK) are pucks a player steals; giveaways (GV) are pucks he loses on his own. Arena scorers log both and vary by rink, so treat them as rough counts.
primaryKeyword: what does gv mean in hockey

name: Games played
short: The number of games a player appeared in. Per-game stats divide by it, and small totals are where the noise lives.
primaryKeyword: what does gp mean in hockey

name: Points per game
short: Points divided by games played. It puts a player who missed time on the same footing as one who played every game, and a point a game marks a star.

name: Penalties drawn
short: Penalties a player draws from opponents, most of them power plays for his team. Drawn minus taken is penalty differential, a small but real piece of a player's value.

name: Save percentage
short: Saves divided by shots on goal faced. It treats a point shot and a backdoor tap-in the same, which is why expected-goals stats grade goalies more fairly.

name: Goals against average
short: Goals a goalie allows per 60 minutes. It ignores how many shots he faced and how dangerous they were, so it grades his defense along with him.

name: Shutouts
short: A game in which a goalie plays the whole way and allows no goals. If two goalies combine for a clean sheet, neither gets credit.
primaryKeyword: what does so mean in hockey

name: Goalie record (W-L-OTL)
short: A goalie's wins, regulation losses and overtime or shootout losses (OTL). The decision goes to the goalie in net for the deciding goal, so it tracks his team too.

name: Goals saved above expected
short: Expected goals a goalie faced minus the goals he allowed. Positive means he stopped more than an average goalie would have on the same shots.

name: Goals saved above average
short: Goals a goalie saved compared with a league-average save percentage on the same number of shots. Unlike GSAx, it treats every shot as equally dangerous.

name: Quality starts
short: A start where a goalie beats the league-average save percentage, or posts .885 on 20 shots or fewer. A really bad start (RBS) is anything under .850.

name: High-danger save percentage
short: Save percentage on high-danger shots only, the shots on goal from right in front of the net. It isolates the saves that swing games, though the samples get small fast.

name: Expected save percentage
short: The save percentage an average goalie would post on the shots a goalie faced, built from expected goals. Subtract it from his real save percentage to see what he added.

name: Saves and shots against
short: Shots against (SA) are shots on goal a goalie faced, goals against (GA) the ones that went in, saves (SV) the rest. Save percentage is SV divided by SA.
primaryKeyword: what does sa mean in hockey

name: Points percentage
short: Standings points earned divided by points available, two per game. It's how you compare teams that have played different numbers of games.
primaryKeyword: what is points percentage in hockey

name: Regulation wins
short: Wins in regulation (RW), or in regulation and overtime (ROW), leaving out shootout wins. When teams finish a season level on points, RW is the first tiebreaker.
primaryKeyword: what does rw mean in hockey

name: Goal differential
short: Goals for minus goals against. Over a full season it tracks standings points closely, which makes it a quick check on whether a record is real.

name: Power play percentage
short: Power-play goals divided by power-play opportunities. It says how well a team converts and nothing about how many power plays it draws.

name: Penalty kill percentage
short: The share of opponents' power plays a team kills off without allowing a goal. It's the mirror image of power-play percentage.

name: Expected goals
short: The probability that an unblocked shot becomes a goal, priced against hundreds of thousands of past NHL shots like it. Add them up for a player's or team's total.

name: Individual expected goals
short: Expected goals on the shots a player takes himself. It measures how many good looks he gets, whether or not they go in.

name: Goals above expected
short: Goals minus expected goals, for a player or team. Positive means the finishing beat an average shooter on the same chances, and a single season carries a lot of luck.

name: Corsi
short: Every shot attempt, on goal, missed or blocked, counted for and against while a player or team is on the ice. CF% is the share; the NHL calls it SAT.

name: Fenwick
short: Corsi without the blocked shots, so unblocked attempts for and against. It's the same set of shots expected goals uses, and the NHL calls it USAT.

name: Relative Corsi
short: A player's Corsi share with him on the ice minus his team's share without him. It shows whether he drives play better or worse than the rest of the roster.

name: PDO
short: On-ice shooting percentage plus on-ice save percentage, usually at five-on-five. Everyone drifts back toward 1.000 (or 100), so a number far from it usually means luck.

name: High-danger chances
short: Shot attempts Natural Stat Trick rates as most dangerous, mostly from right in front of the net, with extra weight for rebounds and rush shots. HDCF% is a team's share.

name: Scoring chances
short: Shot attempts Natural Stat Trick counts as scoring chances, based on where they came from, with extra credit for rebounds and rush shots. SCF% is a team's share.

name: Shot share
short: A team's share of the shots on goal in its games, or in a player's minutes. It's the narrowest shot-share stat, since misses and blocks don't count.

name: Goals for percentage
short: A team's share of the goals scored in its games, or in a player's minutes, usually at five-on-five. It's the result that xGF% and CF% try to predict.

name: On-ice shooting and save percentage
short: The shooting (oiSH%) and save (oiSV%) percentages of a player's team while he's on the ice. Both swing with luck, and their sum is PDO.

name: Zone starts
short: The share of a player's end-zone faceoff starts that came in the offensive zone (OZS%) or his own end (DZS%). Coaches use them to shelter or bury players.

name: Quality of competition and teammates
short: Measures of how strong a player's opponents (QoC) and linemates (QoT) were, usually weighted by shared ice time. They put a player's results in context.

name: Wins above replacement
short: One number for a player's total value over a replacement-level player, in goals (GAR) or wins (WAR). Evolving-Hockey's version also comes in an expected-goals form (xGAR).

name: RAPM
short: Regularized adjusted plus-minus, a regression that estimates each player's impact while controlling for teammates, opponents, zone starts and score. It's a building block of public WAR models.

name: Per-60 rates
short: Any stat divided by ice time and scaled to 60 minutes. It levels the field between a top-line forward and a fourth-liner who plays half as much.

name: Individual points percentage
short: The share of goals scored while a player is on the ice that he scored or assisted on. It shows who's driving the offense and who's along for the ride.

name: Game score
short: A single-game rating that rolls goals, assists, shots, blocks, penalties, faceoffs and on-ice shot and goal results into one number. This site averages MoneyPuck's and HockeyStatCards' versions.

name: Zone entries and exits
short: How a team gets the puck into the offensive zone, carrying it or dumping it in, and how it gets out of its own end. The NHL doesn't log either.

name: Individual shot attempts
short: Every shot attempt a player takes himself, on goal, missed or blocked. It's a pure measure of shooting volume.

name: Score-adjusted stats
short: Stats reweighted for the score, because trailing teams push and leading teams sit back. Unadjusted, a team that leads a lot looks worse at controlling play than it is.

name: Shot quality
short: How dangerous a team's or player's shots are on average, usually expected goals per unblocked attempt. Distance to the net is the biggest single factor.

name: W-Value
short: This site's 0-to-100 rating of a player's value this season, with 50 as the NHL average. Skaters are scored on goals above replacement, goalies on goals saved above expected.

name: Percentile
short: Where a number ranks in its comparison group on a 0-to-100 scale, so the 90th percentile beats 90% of the group. Forwards and defensemen are usually ranked separately here.

name: Five-on-five
short: Both teams with five skaters and a goalie on the ice, which is most of every game. It's the default for comparisons because special-teams time varies so much.

name: Power play and penalty kill (5v4, 4v5)
short: A power play (5v4) is time with an extra skater after an opponent's penalty; the penalty kill (4v5) is the other side. Both are rated here per 60 minutes.

name: All situations
short: Every game state combined, five-on-five, power play, penalty kill, 4-on-4, 3-on-3 and empty net. Individual totals like ixG use it unless a column says otherwise.

name: Expected standings
short: The standings rebuilt on expected goals. Each team's all-situations xGF and xGA become a Pythagorean win rate, then points, and all 32 teams are ranked the same way.

name: Season projection
short: MoneyPuck's simulation of the rest of the season, giving projected points and playoff odds. This site freezes the opening-night projection and shows the updated one, re-run after every result.
